source: arXiv:2507.12843v1 Theorem 7 and Appendix C.3/D.4; v3 Theorem 9 and Appendix C.6
statement: Under both reference-pair alternatives, the same kernel, and the strict squared-embedding-norm ordering, MMD rejection implies NAMMD rejection with the displayed probability lower bound. For C1<=m<=C2 the asymptotic NAMMD-only power advantage is at least 1/65.
assumptions: reference norm sum < test norm sum
acceptance: Every premise and bound in the paper's Gaussian Example 2 is recomputed; the minimum power advantage on the full integer window is >=1/65; reversing the norm ordering destroys the advantage.
